prompt: Many companies now allow their staff to work from home for most of the week. Some people think this arrangement benefits employees, while others argue that it harms teamwork and the training of younger staff. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Home working, which was an emergency measure only a few years ago, has become a permanent arrangement at many firms. Some regard it as a clear improvement in employees' lives, while others believe it undermines collaboration and leaves junior staff without proper training. My own view is that both effects are real, but that they fall on different people.

The benefits to the individual worker are easy to establish. A commute of an hour each way consumes ten hours of an ordinary week, and returning that time to the employee improves sleep, health and family life at no cost to the employer. Home working also removes the low-level interruptions that make concentrated work difficult in an open-plan office, which is why many people report finishing demanding tasks faster at home than in the building they were hired to sit in.

The objection is that the value of an office was never really the desk. Colleagues overhear each other's problems, correct each other's assumptions and pass on judgement that nobody would think to write down. A new graduate learns the unwritten parts of a job by being present while it is done, and scheduled video calls capture almost none of this. Teams also lose the informal contact that resolves small misunderstandings before they become formal disputes.

In my view the arrangement suits experienced staff and disadvantages inexperienced ones. Someone who already knows the work and the people loses very little by leaving the building; someone still learning both loses a great deal. The sensible response is therefore not to choose between the two positions but to apply them differently, requiring far more office attendance in the first years of a career than in the twentieth.
title: Working from home: good for people, bad for teams?
